name: molmo
description: Code for the Molmo Vision-Language Model
editorialSummary: AllenAI’s fully open Molmo VLM: training code and recipes paired with openly released weights and the PixMo dataset family, emphasizing transparency end-to-end.
whyCare: Rare fully open vision-language stack (data + code + weights) from a major lab—strong choice when openness and reproducibility matter.

name: DeepSeek-VL2
description: DeepSeek-VL2: Mixture-of-Experts Vision-Language Models for Advanced Multimodal Understanding
editorialSummary: DeepSeek’s MoE vision-language models for advanced multimodal understanding, succeeding DeepSeek-VL with stronger OCR/document and general visual reasoning.
whyCare: Strong open MoE VLM option from DeepSeek with practical inference code for multimodal agents and document QA.

name: chameleon
description: Repository for Meta Chameleon, a mixed-modal early-fusion foundation model from FAIR.
editorialSummary: Meta FAIR’s early-fusion token-based mixed-modal model that treats images and text in a shared discrete space. Research release; repository is archived.
whyCare: Important architecture reference for early-fusion multimodal transformers beyond encoder-LLM adapters.
notes: Custom Chameleon Research License (GitHub SPDX NOASSERTION). Repo archived.

name: LLaVA
description: [NeurIPS'23 Oral] Visual Instruction Tuning (LLaVA) built towards GPT-4V level capabilities and beyond.
editorialSummary: LLaVA pioneered visual instruction tuning that connects a vision encoder to an LLM with GPT-4-generated multimodal instruction data. It became the default open recipe for GPT-4V-style chat and spawned LLaVA-NeXT and many community fine-tunes.
whyCare: Still the clearest reference implementation for training and serving open vision-language chat models, with widely reused data formats and evaluation setups.

name: LLaVA-NeXT
editorialSummary: Successor codebase to classic LLaVA with stronger image understanding, higher-resolution inputs, and video/multimodal extensions under the LLaVA-VL org. Prefer this over the original LLaVA repo for newer checkpoints and training scripts.
whyCare: Active LLaVA-family training and inference stack used for LLaVA-NeXT / OneVision-style open VLMs.

name: PhiCookBook
description: This is a Phi Family of SLMs book for getting started with Phi Models. Phi a family of open sourced AI models developed by Microsoft. Phi models are the most capable and cost-effective small language models (SLMs) available, outperforming models of the same size and next size up across a variety of language, reasoning, coding, and math benchmarks
editorialSummary: Official Microsoft cookbook for Phi SLMs with dedicated guidance for Phi-3/3.5 vision and Phi-4 multimodal—prompting, fine-tuning, and deployment patterns for vision-language use.
whyCare: Best open starting point for Phi-3 Vision / Phi multimodal OSS workflows when weights are consumed via Azure, Hugging Face, or ONNX.
notes: Repo renamed from Phi-3CookBook; covers Phi vision/multimodal chapters. Model weights are published separately on Hugging Face / Azure.

name: unilm
description: Large-scale Self-supervised Pre-training Across Tasks, Languages, and Modalities
editorialSummary: Microsoft’s long-running multimodal/NLP research monorepo. Contains Kosmos-1, Kosmos-2, and Kosmos-2.5 code alongside LayoutLM, BEiT, TrOCR, and other foundation models.
whyCare: Canonical open source for Kosmos grounded multimodal models and related Microsoft document/vision-language research code.
notes: Kosmos family directories: kosmos-1, kosmos-2, kosmos-2.5 inside this monorepo. Activity verification 2026-08-12: maintenance moderate→slow (pushedAt=2026-01-23T04:09:35Z, primary_status=low_activity).

name: open_clip
description: An open source implementation of CLIP.
editorialSummary: Community CLIP implementation with many pretrained backbones (LAION, DataComp, SigLIP-style training), scalable training scripts, and active releases—preferred over openai/CLIP for new embedding work.
whyCare: De-facto open CLIP training/inference library with far more checkpoints and training options than the original OpenAI repo.
notes: GitHub license API reports NOASSERTION; LICENSE file is MIT.

name: CLIP
description: CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining),  Predict the most relevant text snippet given an image
editorialSummary: OpenAI’s original contrastive language-image pretraining code and ViT/ResNet checkpoints. Foundation of modern zero-shot vision, retrieval, and many VLM vision towers.
whyCare: Still the baseline embedding/zero-shot API everyone compares against; required literacy for multimodal work.

name: MiniCPM-V
description: A Pocket-Sized MLLM for Ultra-Efficient Image and Video Understanding on Your Phone
editorialSummary: OpenBMB’s efficient multimodal LLM series (MiniCPM-V / MiniCPM-o) aimed at strong image and video understanding on edge devices and phones, with frequent model drops.
whyCare: Top pick when you need capable open multimodal models that actually fit consumer GPUs or mobile deployment budgets.

name: InternVL
description: [CVPR 2024 Oral] InternVL Family: A Pioneering Open-Source Alternative to GPT-4o.  接近GPT-4o表现的开源多模态对话模型
editorialSummary: OpenGVLab’s InternVL family scales vision backbones and multimodal chat models as an open GPT-4o-class alternative, with strong docs and a wide model ladder.
whyCare: High-performing open MLLM stack with clear training/inference paths and competitive multimodal benchmarks.

name: Qwen-VL
description: The official repo of Qwen-VL (通义千问-VL) chat & pretrained large vision language model proposed by Alibaba Cloud.
editorialSummary: Original Tongyi Qianwen vision-language release that established the Qwen-VL line. Kept for historical reference and older checkpoints; prefer Qwen3-VL for current models.
whyCare: Important baseline and paper code for early open Chinese/English VLMs; useful when reproducing older Qwen-VL results.
notes: GitHub license API reports NOASSERTION; repo ships Tongyi Qianwen LICENSE AGREEMENT (not SPDX).

name: Qwen3-VL
description: Qwen3-VL is the multimodal large language model series developed by Qwen team, Alibaba Cloud.
editorialSummary: Official Qwen vision-language series repo (GitHub redirects older Qwen2-VL / Qwen2.5-VL URLs here). Covers Alibaba’s current open multimodal LLMs with strong OCR, document, and video understanding.
whyCare: One of the strongest open VLM families for production multimodal apps; this is the canonical training/inference home for the latest Qwen-VL line.
notes: QwenLM/Qwen2-VL and QwenLM/Qwen2.5-VL resolve to this repo on GitHub. Activity verification 2026-08-12: maintenance moderate→slow (pushedAt=2026-01-30T04:47:30Z, primary_status=low_activity).

name: LAVIS
description: LAVIS - A One-stop Library for Language-Vision Intelligence
editorialSummary: Salesforce’s unified library for vision-language research, including BLIP, BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, ALBEF, and related tasks (captioning, VQA, retrieval). Primary open home for BLIP-2 training and inference APIs.
whyCare: If you need BLIP-2 or a batteries-included VL research framework (datasets, trainers, evals), LAVIS is the standard package.
notes: BLIP-2 lives in this library; there is no separate official Salesforce/blip2 application repo. Activity verification 2026-08-12: maintenance active→moderate (pushedAt=2026-06-02T18:14:49Z, primary_status=maintained).

name: MiniGPT-4
description: Open-sourced codes for MiniGPT-4 and MiniGPT-v2 (https://minigpt-4.github.io, https://minigpt-v2.github.io/)
editorialSummary: Early open GPT-4V-style system aligning a frozen vision encoder with Vicuna via a projection layer. MiniGPT-v2 extended grounded conversation; highly influential for lightweight VLM recipes.
whyCare: Classic minimal recipe for vision-language chat; still cited and forked for teaching and rapid prototyping.
